claim: Ahead of the first automated sweep, the agent changed the input lock-in's sensitivity from an inherited 2 microvolt full-scale setting (which would rail on any kilo-ohm-scale resistance) to 1 millivolt with an autorange hook, and reduced the time constant from 0.3 s at 24 dB/oct to 30 ms on both signal lock-ins, trading noise floor for point rate on the liveness sweep.
context: At bring-up, the restorable acquisition-state snapshot showed sensitivity and time-constant settings inherited from a prior configuration that were unsuited to the resistances expected on this pair; the agent proposed the change and flagged it to the operator before executing the first automated sweep.
evidence: State-capture snapshot values (sr1 sensitivity 2 microvolt, tau 0.3 s/24 dB per oct); planned replacement values (1 millivolt autorange, tau 30 ms) recorded in the plan file and the pre-grant summary text.

claim: After the liveness sweep, the agent raised the lock-in time constant from 30 ms to 100 ms (delay 0.5 s) for the following back-gate sweep, judging the faster setting too noisy to keep using.
context: The liveness sweep showed a periodic ripple on the current and phase channels attributed to interference through the 30 ms filter; the agent slowed down before running the next sweep, roughly doubling the per-point dwell time.
evidence: Noise description (about plus/minus 50 ohm on a few-microvolt signal with periodic ripple) tied to the 30 ms filter; the following sweep's tau/delay set to 100 ms / 0.5 s.

claim: The contact pair was judged alive and ohmic over a full top-gate sweep at zero back-gate voltage, with the longitudinal resistance running only about 40-370 ohm and no charge-neutrality peak in that cut; the monotonic resistance trend was read as the device being electron-doped at zero back-gate voltage, with the neutrality point lying outside the swept top-gate window.
context: First automated sweep of the session: a top-gate sweep and back at zero back-gate, field, and Si-gate voltage, used to establish contact continuity, resistance scale, and per-point timing before committing to longer sweeps.
evidence: Drain current 9.92 nA at 172 degree phase, stable to 1%; resistance trace 40-370 ohm with a weak hump near -0.2 V top-gate; no hysteresis between up/down legs.

claim: Because the neutrality point was not found in the top-gate cut, the agent chose to sweep the back gate next (at zero top-gate voltage) rather than go straight to a full 2D map, reasoning from a geometry-based lever-arm estimate that the back gate reaches further into the hole side and would be the cheaper way to locate the neutrality point.
context: Decision made immediately after reading the liveness sweep's result, before committing to a roughly 30-minute full-box map.
evidence: Geometry-prior estimate that the back gate reaches a carrier density on the order of -2e12 per square centimeter at its negative rail, cited as the reason to try a 1D back-gate sweep before a 2D map.

claim: The back-gate sweep showed two distinct resistance maxima (roughly 310 ohm and 275 ohm) straddling zero back-gate voltage, reproducible with no hysteresis, with peak contrast only about 3x over the metallic background; the agent flagged two competing explanations -- two parallel neutrality lines from doping inhomogeneity between the voltage-probe contacts, versus a single neutrality point plus a separate band-edge feature that would diverge from it at finite displacement field -- to be resolved by a 2D gate map.
context: Established right after the back-gate sweep completed, by inspection of the two peak positions/heights and their gate-voltage separation, before the coarse 2D map was designed to discriminate between the two readings.
evidence: Peak positions and heights (~310 ohm, ~275 ohm) and separation (~0.37 V back-gate voltage, ~0.56e12 per square centimeter by geometry); comparison of up/down sweep legs.

claim: The agent designed a coarse 2D gate map across the full accessible gate box (back gate stepped slowly, top gate stepped fast at a finer resolution) specifically to trace the displacement-field dependence of the resistance peak, on the reasoning that an exponential rise with |D| would indicate one candidate stacking order, a modest field-symmetric rise another, and a field-asymmetric rise the third -- making this map the session's first stacking-order discriminator.
context: Planned immediately after the back-gate sweep, before running any 2D map, using a table of expected displacement-field signatures for the three candidate stacking orders drawn up earlier in the session.
evidence: Sweep design: back gate as the slow axis, top gate as the fast axis at finer resolution than the slow axis; explicit discriminator table (rise shape and field-symmetry per candidate) motivating the map.

claim: From the coarse map, the agent fitted a single neutrality ridge across the box, extracted a gate-capacitance ratio about 20% below the geometry-based estimate, and found the on-ridge resistance rising about ninefold from roughly 320 ohm near zero displacement field to about 2.8 kilohm at higher field, then saturating -- read as 'nowhere near insulating' -- with the two field signs roughly symmetric within the coarse sampling, plus a second, weaker, field-flat resistance ridge offset in gate voltage from the main one, read as either a second doped region or a hole-side band feature not yet distinguishable.
context: Established from the completed coarse 2D map by locating the ridge of maximum resistance row by row and fitting its slope and displacement-field trend; an earlier attempt at this same map crashed a live-plotting subprocess and was discarded, and this reading comes from the successful relaunch.
evidence: Ridge fit giving a gate-capacitance ratio about 20% below the geometry prior; on-ridge resistance values (~320 ohm near zero field rising to ~2.8 kilohm, saturating 2.7-2.85 kilohm over the upper part of the field range); comparable peak resistances on the mirrored negative-field rows; a second ridge ~300-350 ohm offset by roughly half a volt in back-gate voltage that does not converge with the main ridge.

claim: Based on the modest, saturating, roughly field-symmetric rise of the on-ridge resistance (up to about ninefold but no sign of the sharp exponential rise expected for one candidate stacking order), the agent's intermediate read after the coarse map leaned toward a Bernal-like stacking assignment.
context: Stated as a running lean at the end of the coarse-map analysis, prior to the finer band map and the field-dependent measurements that would follow.
evidence: Comparison of the observed saturating rise against the discriminator table's exponential-rise expectation for the excluded candidate.

claim: The agent designed a finer raster (a narrower top-gate window at higher resolution, co-swept with a moderate back-gate step) that followed the ridge fitted from the coarse map, spanning most of the back-gate range on both carrier signs, specifically to resolve the peak resistance and width versus displacement field and to get a cleaner positive/negative field comparison than the coarse map's edge-pinned negative side allowed.
context: Designed immediately after the coarse-map read, to address its two open questions: resistance and width versus field at finer resolution, and the field-sign comparison free of box-edge clipping.
evidence: Sweep design: raster in a narrow window about the fitted ridge line, at higher gate resolution than the coarse map, covering both field signs; rows clipped to stay inside the accessible box.

claim: The fine map refit the neutrality-ridge slope (giving an updated gate-capacitance ratio that supersedes the coarse-map estimate) and located the true resistance minimum, which the agent adopted as the session's displacement-field-zero reference point; referenced to that point, the negative-to-positive field resistance ratio was about 0.85-0.90 over the reachable overlapping range -- read as no sign of a strong field-sign asymmetry -- while the positive side climbed about fourteenfold to roughly 3.4 kilohm before saturating flat to the edge of the sweep, and the peak narrowed from a broad ~150-220 mV window near the reference point to a sharp ~45 mV once gapped.
context: Established from the completed fine raster by re-locating the ridge minimum, computing the resistance ratio between mirrored displacement-field points, and comparing peak widths near versus away from the reference point.
evidence: New ridge fit and gate-capacitance ratio; resistance minimum value and its gate-voltage coordinates; negative/positive resistance ratio over a stated field-offset range; peak-width narrowing from ~150-220 mV to ~45 mV.

claim: The agent read the fine map as essentially field-symmetric (excluding the field-asymmetric candidate stacking order), showing no exponential/insulating gap up to the edge of the sweep (excluding the strongly-gapping candidate), and showing a broad two-carrier neutrality region at the field-zero reference point with a modest, saturating displacement-field-induced gap -- overall consistent with the Bernal-like candidate, pending confirmation from the planned field-dependent Landau-level measurements and the temperature-activation ladder.
context: Stated as the updated stacking lean immediately after the fine-map analysis, explicitly left open pending the field-dependent and temperature-dependent measurements still to come.
evidence: Field-symmetry ratio, absence of an exponential/insulating rise, and the two-carrier peak-shape argument, combined per the discriminator table drawn up earlier in the session.

claim: The agent chose to measure the field-dependent Landau structure near the displacement-field reference point by ramping the magnet continuously to a chosen field cap while co-sweeping the gates along the fixed-displacement-field line through the reference point every row, binning on the field value recorded at each point during analysis, rather than stepping the field and holding for each row -- trading field-per-row resolution for finishing within the bare ramp time.
context: Designed once the field-zero reference point and the gate-capacitance ratio were in hand from the fine map, to get the Landau-level sequence near neutrality (identified as the discriminator between two of the candidate stacking orders) and to calibrate the absolute carrier-density scale from the Landau-level line slopes.
evidence: Continuous-ramp method description (rows slanted by a fraction of a tesla, binned on measured field); chosen field cap within the instrument's committed limit; step size and approximate row/point counts for the co-swept gate line.

claim: When the first attempt at the field-ramp sweep failed on a data-writer bug after the ramp had already been started, the agent chose to relaunch the same measurement riding the ramp in progress from its current field (about 0.7 T) rather than pay several minutes returning the magnet to zero field first, accepting the loss of the lowest-field portion of the sweep on the judgment that the lost interval was below where the Landau levels of interest would be resolvable.
context: Made immediately after diagnosing the writer failure (a data-type serialization bug, not an instrument or physics problem) and confirming the magnet was still ramping toward the target field.
evidence: Stated field at relaunch (about 0.7 T out of an 8 T target); stated rationale that the lost 0-0.7 T interval is below the resolvable Landau-level range; row count re-sized to the remaining field span.

claim: A single scale factor fit to roughly 257 resistance-minima positions gave a carrier-density calibration about 18% below the geometry-based estimate (consistent with the gate-capacitance-ratio discrepancy found earlier); on that scale the minima cluster in steps of four, with the +/-4 levels tracked down to the lowest resolvable fields -- read as the single-particle degenerate Landau-level sequence of one candidate stacking order rather than the alternative candidate's expected pattern, which would instead show its lowest robust levels only at higher filling factor.
context: Established from the completed field-ramp sweep by fitting all resistance-minima positions to Landau-level index times field, using the field values recorded per point during the ramp; compared against the candidate stacking orders' predicted level sequences drawn up earlier in the session.
evidence: Fitted density-scale factor (about 0.82x the geometry estimate) from about 257 minima; filling-factor sequence in steps of four; lowest field at which the +/-4 levels are resolved.

claim: The zero-filling-factor state's resistance grew with field but non-monotonically, showing two field windows where it dipped rather than rose (once around 2.2-2.5 T and again around 6.7-7.3 T); the agent read these dips as Landau-level crossings within the zero-energy manifold characteristic of the same candidate stacking order favored above, contrasting with the alternative candidate's expectation of monotonic growth.
context: Read directly from the zero-filling-factor resistance trace versus field in the completed field-ramp sweep, immediately following the level-sequence fit.
evidence: Zero-filling-factor resistance values at the two dip windows (roughly 47 to 39 kilohm and 794 to 775 kilohm).

claim: Combining the Landau-level sequence, the zero-filling-factor crossing pattern, and the earlier gate-map findings, the agent's running stacking read after this field-ramp sweep was reinforced toward the same Bernal-like candidate, with a second field-dependent sweep at finite displacement field and the temperature-activation ladder still to come.
context: Stated as an updated running lean immediately after the field-ramp sweep's analysis.
evidence: Combination of the level-spacing and zero-state-crossing findings with the prior gate-map symmetry and gap-saturation findings.

claim: Rather than ramp back to zero field and re-ramp at a different gate setting, the agent used the necessary field descent from the cap to measure a second field-dependent sweep along a gate line at a finite displacement field corresponding to the knee of the field-independent resistance plateau identified earlier, on the reasoning that this would test both the Landau-level structure of the gapped state and whether the zero-field plateau was carrying its own parallel conduction path.
context: Planned once the first field-ramp sweep reached the field cap, using the earlier fine-map result for which gate setting corresponds to the plateau knee, and justified explicitly by a policy of never re-traversing the field for free.
evidence: Choice of gate line based on the fine map's plateau-knee point; step size and approximate row/point counts for the descent; explicit statement of the two purposes (Landau structure of the gapped state, and the parallel-path question).

claim: Using the density calibration from the first field-ramp sweep with no free parameters, the second sweep's roughly 204 resistance minima fell in steps of two rather than four, read as the displacement field lifting a two-fold degeneracy of the Landau levels; the zero-filling-factor state now grew monotonically with field, with no crossings, consistent with the field having polarized the zero-energy manifold rather than leaving it in the crossing regime seen at zero displacement field.
context: Established from the completed second field-dependent sweep (at finite displacement field) using the calibration fixed by the first sweep; read together with an earlier mid-sweep checkpoint that had already shown a healthy, leakage-free descent.
evidence: Filling-factor sequence in steps of two; zero-filling-factor resistance rising monotonically from about 1 kilohm to about 73 kilohm over the field range; contrast with the non-monotonic zero-state trace at zero displacement field.

claim: The zero-filling-factor resistance trace extrapolated smoothly down to the same few-kilohm value already seen as the zero-field plateau at that displacement field, and no other electronic system's signature appeared anywhere in the swept density window; the agent read this as showing the zero-field plateau is a property of the same gapped channel (finite conduction below the gap at the operating temperature) rather than an independent parallel conduction path, leaving the temperature ladder to make the final call on activation versus residual conduction.
context: Read from the low-field end of the second field-dependent sweep, comparing the extrapolated zero-field resistance to the previously measured field-free value at the same gate setting.
evidence: Extrapolated versus previously measured zero-field resistance value at the same displacement-field point; absence of any additional resistance feature across the fan's density window.

claim: The agent's running stacking read after the second field-dependent sweep remained the same Bernal-like candidate, now additionally supported by the displacement-field-split, two-fold Landau-level sequence and the monotonic, field-polarized zero-filling-factor state.
context: Stated as the updated running lean immediately after the second field-dependent sweep's analysis, with only the temperature-activation ladder remaining before the final call.
evidence: Combination of the two-fold split sequence and monotonic zero-state trend with all preceding gate-map and first-sweep findings.

claim: The agent designed a temperature ladder from base temperature up to 50 K, at five displacement-field points spanning the reference point and both gapped and near-neutral settings identified by the fine map, to measure the thermal activation of the field-induced gap and settle whether it matches the meV scale expected for one candidate stacking order or the much larger scale expected for another, and separately to determine whether the zero-field plateau's resistance is thermally activated (a real gap) or temperature-independent (a residual/parallel conduction path).
context: Planned once both field-dependent sweeps were complete and the evidence chain still left the size and thermal character of the field-induced gap, and the nature of the zero-field plateau, unresolved.
evidence: Ten temperature setpoints from base to 50 K with a fixed heater ratio and a stability-acceptance window; five displacement-field windows chosen at the fine map's field-offset points, run as one combined sweep per temperature.

claim: Partway through the temperature ladder, the neutrality-point resistance was flat with temperature at every displacement-field point measured so far, including the most gapped point, up to about 7 K; the agent read this as showing no activation yet on the range measured, with the decisive temperature range (roughly 9-50 K, where a meV-scale gap would be expected to show a resistance drop) still ahead.
context: Read from the first several temperature-ladder points partway through the ladder, comparing the neutrality-point resistance at each field setting across the temperatures measured so far to the corresponding thermal energy scale.
evidence: Neutrality-point resistance values held roughly constant across the first several temperature points at each of the five field settings, compared to the corresponding thermal energy scale.

claim: Across the full temperature ladder, the neutrality-point resistance stayed flat with temperature below about 7 K at every displacement-field point, then fell gently at the two most-gapped points, giving Arrhenius activation energies of roughly 1.8 meV and 1.2 meV at those two points and essentially no activation (flat or slightly rising resistance) at the reference point and the two more weakly gapped points; the gap scale was read as meV-sized and only weakly dependent on displacement field, with a large non-vanishing resistance extrapolated to infinite temperature, consistent with thermally assisted conduction over a small, saturating gap and specifically excluding the tens-of-meV activation energy and order-of-magnitude resistance collapse expected for one candidate stacking order (a roughly threefold change was observed instead).
context: Established from the complete temperature ladder by fitting an Arrhenius slope to the neutrality-point resistance above about 8 K at each of the five displacement-field points and comparing to the candidates' predicted activation-energy scales.
evidence: Resistance values at the two most-gapped points falling from a few kilohm at base temperature to roughly a third of that by 50 K; fitted activation energies (~1.8 meV and ~1.2 meV); flat/rising resistance at the other three points; large residual resistance extrapolated to infinite temperature.

claim: The temperature ladder's result -- non-activated behavior at the reference and weakly-gapped points, and only modest, saturating activation at the two most-gapped points -- was read as confirming that the zero-field resistance plateau seen earlier is a property of the small-gap channel itself (finite, thermally assisted sub-gap conduction) rather than an external parallel-conduction path.
context: Stated as the resolution of the open parallel-path question raised during the second field-dependent sweep's analysis, once the full temperature-ladder data set was in hand.
evidence: Comparison of the ladder's activation behavior at the gapped points against the alternative (temperature-independent, parallel-path) expectation.

claim: The weak, field-flat secondary resistance ridge seen offset from the main neutrality line in the back-gate sweep and the coarse map, which showed no Landau-level signature of its own in either field-dependent sweep, was read by the agent as most consistent with a contact-doped strip near a voltage probe rather than a second stacking domain in the measured region, though this attribution was not directly imaged and could not be confirmed.
context: Assessed at the final call by combining the zero-field gate-map appearance of the secondary ridge with its absence of any distinguishable signature in either of the two field-dependent sweeps.
evidence: Secondary ridge's resistance scale and gate-voltage offset from the main neutrality line seen in the zero-field sweeps; absence of a corresponding feature in either field-dependent sweep's Landau-level analysis.

claim: The agent's final call for the one measured contact pair was Bernal (ABAB) stacking, stated as a strong determination, based on the combined evidence chain from the session: a saturating, meV-scale, field-symmetric neutrality-point gap; a four-fold degenerate Landau-level sequence with zero-state crossings at zero displacement field; a displacement-field-split two-fold sequence with a monotonic zero-state at finite displacement field; and the temperature-activation results -- all evaluated on the session's own in-session density and displacement-field calibration. No other region of the device was measurable this session, since every other spare contact pair was dead or unconnected as provided, so the call is explicitly scoped to the single measured region.
context: Delivered as the final entry of the session's analysis record, after all planned measurements (gate maps, both field-dependent sweeps, and the temperature ladder) were complete, closing out the evidence chain built up over the session.
evidence: Full evidence chain: neutrality-point gap and field-symmetry from the gate maps; Landau-level sequence and zero-state behavior from both field-dependent sweeps; activation energies from the temperature ladder; in-session density and displacement-field-ratio calibration values. Stated would-overturn conditions: a much larger activation gap at reachable displacement field, strong field-sign asymmetry, or a level sequence starting at higher filling factor -- all explicitly excluded by the session's data. Stated as not excludable by symmetry alone: an accidentally compensated asymmetric-stacking scenario, though the level-sequence evolution and zero-state pattern were judged to match the stated candidate specifically.
